summary: Nora now sees message edits on Signal, WhatsApp, Instagram and Discord, and reads an edited message as a correction rather than a second message.
details: An edit is recorded beside the message it changes. The transcript shows the latest text where the message was originally sent, with when it was edited and what it first said.
Instagram and Discord edits reach Nora for the first time; Signal and WhatsApp edits no longer appear as a duplicate, unmarked message.
Honcho is told about an edit as a correction of what the person first said, not as a new, independent statement.

An edit opens a turn only when it newly addresses Nora — adding an @-mention or her trigger to a message that had none. Fixing a typo in a message that already tagged her does not make her answer again.
limitations: Deleted or unsent messages are still not captured.
An edit to a message Nora never recorded (older than her retention window, or from before she was in the room) is ignored.
If someone edits a question Nora already answered, she does not answer again; she sees the corrected text on her next turn.
Signal and WhatsApp edits received before this release stay in the transcript as separate messages until they age out of the window.
An edit to a message sent before this release never opens a turn, because Nora has no record of whom that message mentioned.
